summary: Week 5 check-in on Redwood Private pilot. Main topics: kernel upgrade canary, intermittent 95th percentile latency spikes correlated with topology churn, KV cache miss rate increase after NTP drift incident, and routing fallback tuning. Agreed to run a focused perf harness and dry-run the network runbook before the next canary. Action items assigned to Priya, Maya, and Alex.

Can Redwood support local KMS with HSM integration for pilot?
Is there an automated test for prefix KV caching across restarts?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-24 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Walker (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood Support), Jordan Lee (Orchid CTO), Maya Patel (Orchid NetEng), Samir Reddy (Orchid DevOps), Elena Gomez (Orchid PM)

Auto-summary (brief): Priya walked through kernel upgrade plan, we reviewed telemetry showing a 95th spike on 8/22 coincident with a topology change, Maya explained net changes, Samir agreed to run perf harness v2, next steps captured.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: All right team, thanks for joining, uh let's do a quick round robin on who's here, and then Priya will kick off with the kernel canary plan.
[00:18] Jordan: Jordan here, hey thanks. We have Maya, Samir, and Elena on.
[00:24] Maya: Maya, NetEng. Quick note, we had a small overlay change on the 22nd but it was supposed to be non disruptive.
[00:31] Priya: Great, thanks. I'll share my screen in a sec. The goal today is to confirm the canary window for the kernel/quant update and to align on circuit breaker thresholds for the routing fallback.
[00:42] Samir: Before you go on, do we have a clear rollback plan? Last time the canary took a while to roll back due to KV cache warmup.
[00:48] Priya: Yes, good call. We have a staged rollback: quick abort at request router level, then node drain and image revert. The tricky bit is the KV cache warmup, we saw a 10-12% cold miss deltas — or "K-V cash" in the logs, apologies for the transcript weirdness — after a full revert. So we plan to keep an overlap period where both kernels run and use prefix caching to avoid cold path.
[01:12] Alex: Also note we'll push a config that prolongs the KV cache TTL for 30 minutes during rollback to mitigate.
[01:20] Maya: That TTL tweak helped on the staging tests, but on prod we still saw 200–300ms tail. The 8/22 spike — I pulled the traces — coincided with an overlay reconvergence and an NTP drift on one of the hosts. Might be two interacting issues.
[01:38] Priya: Yeah, our telemetry shows increased gRPC retry counts at the same timestamps. Could be inter-node heartbeat timeouts exacerbated by the kernel scheduler change.
[01:46] Liam: To add, support flagged a pattern where the KV miss rate rose after the pod restarts, and some clients fell back to the hosted model which added latency.
[01:56] Jordan: Hosted fallback was surprising to us — we expected Redwood Private to keep requests local. Is that intended behavior?
[02:03] Alex: It's intended as a safety fallback but it's configurable by policy. Priya, can you describe the routing policy we suggested?
[02:10] Priya: Sure: default is local-only for the pilot, but we had an emergency rule that allows hosted fallback if node pool health < 70% for > 2 minutes. We can tighten that to 50% and extend the window to 5 minutes; that reduces unnecessary outbound failovers.
[02:27] Maya: I prefer tightening. Outbound is a hard compliance no for certain tenants here.
[02:32] Elena: To be explicit, the compliance team requires an auditable log of any outbound fallback.
[02:37] Alex: We'll include fallback events in the audit log and ship the sample JSON we talked about.
[02:41] Samir: Back to perf, can we schedule a perf harness run that simulates the overlay reconverge? Last time our reconverge load pattern wasn't well represented.
[02:49] Priya: Yes, Priya: we built a harness version 2 that includes jitter + simulated NTP drift and overlay flaps. We recommend running 10k requests at varying concurrency and collecting p50/p95/p99 and KV miss rates.
[03:05] Jordan: How long will that take? We want results before the canary on Monday.
[03:10] Priya: The run itself is about 45 minutes to an hour; analysis maybe another 2–3 hours. If you run it tonight we can parse in the morning.
[03:17] Maya: We'll run it tonight. We'll need the exact test plan and the endpoint list.
[03:22] Alex: I'll drop the harness YAML and the endpoint set to the shared drive after the call.
[03:26] Priya: Quick note on the kernel change: this is the quant-2 path — it flips a different matmul kernel and changes how we manage attention key/value cache alignment. In practice that's what reduced throughput variance in staging, but it interacts with scheduler latency on older NICs.
[03:44] Samir: NICs are Broadcom 57414, some 2-year old firmware. Is there a minimum NIC firmware you recommend?
[03:50] Priya: We recommend the 1.12.x firmware or newer. We have a short compatibility matrix in the doc.
[03:56] Maya: Ok we'll check upgrade windows.
[04:00] Alex: Security question that came up from your GRC: can Redwood integrate with your on-prem HSM?
[04:05] Priya: Short answer yes; we support KMIP and can plug into HSM-backed KMS. For the pilot we usually do customer-managed keys in a VM with encryption-at-rest, but we can prepare an HSM guide.
[04:16] Elena: Great — also need SOC2 scoping answers.
[04:19] Alex: I'll share the SOC2 scoping doc and a prefilled questionnaire by EOW.
[04:25] Jordan: Back to routing: we saw two incidents of partial failover where individual routes fell back but the cluster was still nominal. Is route pinning something you support?
[04:34] Priya: We do per-route affinity and we can pin critical routes to dedicated node pools. That is already in the current config for the patient-ident route. We can expand to additional high-compliance routes.
[04:44] Maya: Pinning is good, but it reduces our effective capacity so we need realistic SLOs.
[04:49] Priya: We can run a capacity estimate post-pin and suggest autoscale configs.
[04:54] Samir: One operational nit — when the KV cache warms it uses more memory and triggers eviction in other processes. Have you measured memory overhead after kernel change?
[05:03] Priya: In canary staging we saw a 5–8% memory uptick on avg per model instance; not huge but noticeable on constrained nodes. We suggest increasing node memory by one tier or reducing per-instance worker count by one during canary.
[05:16] Maya: We can allocate two nodes as buffer for the canary.
[05:19] Alex: Nice. Ok let's talk schedule: Priya, when would you like to roll the kernel canary?
[05:25] Priya: If Orchid runs the harness tonight and shares results tomorrow morning, we can start a canary on Friday 02:00 PT with a 2-hour window. If the telemetry looks good, expand Saturday and full rollout early next week.
[05:37] Jordan: Friday 02:00 is doable. We want a dry-run of the network runbook before the canary.
[05:41] Alex: Let's schedule runbook dry-run Wednesday 09:00 PT.
[05:45] Elena: Wednesday works. Please send invite and prep steps.
[05:49] Priya: I'll own the runbook dry-run and bring the support triage playbook. Liam will be on the pager if anything pops.
[05:57] Liam: yep I'll be on call.
[06:00] Samir: A few smaller asks — can we get a sample fallback policy and the audit log format? Also the exact timing of the kernel rollback window?
[06:07] Alex: Yes, shim those: fallback policy and audit sample JSON will be uploaded; rollback window: we allow a quick abort for 15 minutes with automated throttle, then a controlled node drain which takes up to 45 minutes total for a full revert. We'll encode these in the checklist.
[06:24] Maya: That 45 minutes is acceptable. One more telemetry question: the trace IDs we saw on 8/22 had truncated spans in our collector — any idea why?
[06:33] Priya: Likely due to the tracer library version mismatch; our SDK used 1.8 while your collector expected 1.6. We have a compatibility note in the instrumentation guide; recommend aligning to 1.8 or using the shim we provided.
[06:47] Jordan: Okay we'll align versions.
[06:50] Alex: Cool — any blockers left?
[06:53] Elena: None from PM, just need the docs and invites.
[06:56] Samir: I'll run harness tonight and upload results.
[07:00] Priya: Perfect. We'll reconvene after results; if everything is green we'll do the canary Friday 02:00 PT.
[07:06] Alex: Great thanks everyone. Recap of action items and owners in the notes, we'll share folder link. Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
